cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll lend you the ladder for two lifts to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need it for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. One lift, then. And tell your wife my roses have improved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds. Three if you say we're still friends when you hand it over.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets terms and A3 controls questions, but A5 ordinary price quote does not distinctly maintain superiority beyond bargaining.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 short duration causes A3 reduced lift demand; B4 cash request causes A5 priced reassurance, while A3 restriction addresses no question.

relationship.evidence: B2 limits the favor and B4 offers simpler payment, giving A credible counteroffers to negotiate.

heightening.evidence: B4 cash solution becomes A5 another chance to price friendship rather than ending the bargaining.

specificity.evidence: A1 ladder and station lifts establish a neighbor favor, with B2 five-minute use clarifying scale.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 friendship discount is earned by B4 cash proposal; A3 authority wording slows the exchange.
